deep.reconstruction:
Context from the previous page. Grothendieck classifies holomorphic spheres Σ carrying an automorphism u of order 2 and a marked set K = {P} ⊔ I. Here P is a fixed point of u, called ∞, and I consists of two u-orbits of non-fixed points, so |I| = 4. The other fixed point is 0. Then T_1 = Σ∖{0,∞} is a C^*-torsor, T_1 = L_1^* for a vector line L_1. The two ±1-orbits in T_1 become a pair {ξ,η} of distinct points of T_2 = T_1^{∧2}. Their product e = ξ∧η lies in T_4 ≅ L_1^{⊗4∗} and trivialises T_4. This reduces the structure group of T_1 from C^* to μ_4. The datum {ξ,η} is then equivalent to the pair (e, ξ+η) subject to the discriminant condition (ξ+η)^2 − 4e ≠ 0.

This page rigidifies by choosing e_1 ∈ T_1 with e_1^{∧4} = e, i.e. a μ_4-trivialisation; the letter ξ on this page is an overloaded name for a fourth root of unity ζ. In the induced coordinate on T_2 (basis e_1^{∧2}), the pair becomes {λ,μ} with λμ = 1. Replacing e_1 by ζe_1 (ζ^4 = 1) changes {λ,μ} into {ζ^2 λ, ζ^2 μ}. So the invariant s = λ+μ is unchanged for ζ = ±1 and changes sign for ζ = ±i.

The rigidified moduli space is therefore the s-line, minus s = ±2 (where λ = μ, i.e. the two orbits collide) and minus ∞. Grothendieck also removes 0 and obtains P^1∖{0,±2,∞}, a four-punctured sphere. The unrigidified moduli orbicurve is its quotient by s ↦ −s (coordinate t = s^2), with the residual μ_2 = ⟨u⟩ as generic stabiliser.

Forgetting u and keeping the 5 marked points (∞ and the four points of I) gives a map to M_{0,5}. The image is a 1-dimensional 'special locus': the locus of 5-pointed spheres with an involution fixing one marked point. Grothendieck proposes to study the induced map on fundamental groupoids, i.e. how this sub-orbicurve sits in the Teichmüller tower and interacts with the Galois action. The next page begins a 'catalogue of elementary operations' in RTD_top (rigidified Teichmüller data). So this page serves the programme of generating the Teichmüller tower in low dimension from modular orbicurves with symmetry.
errors: The removal of s = 0 is not forced by the geometry. s = 0 corresponds to the configuration {±a, ±ia, ∞}, which is a legitimate 5-pointed sphere with the given involution, with extra Z/4 symmetry z ↦ iz. It is excluded only if ξ+η is required to be a point of the torsor T_2 rather than of the line L_2. So P^1∖{0,±2,∞} is the locus avoiding the extra-symmetric point; the full rigidified space is A^1∖{±2}, and s = 0 is an orbifold point of the quotient.
Notation clash: ξ denotes both a point of T_2 (previous page) and the fourth root of unity on this page.

ideas.what: Describing spheres with an involution and marked orbits via C^*-torsors, tensor powers T^{∧n} and reduction of structure group to μ_4.
ideas.modern_name: Moduli of curves with automorphism / special loci, via line-bundle (torsor) coordinates
ideas.usually_credited_to: Special loci in M_{0,n}: Schneps (2003), Collas–Maugeais (2010s); cyclic covers: classical
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme mentions modular orbicurves with symmetry, but not this computation

ideas.what: Rigidified moduli of such structures is P^1 minus 4 points (s = λ+1/λ, s ≠ ±2), with a μ_2 action s ↦ −s, mapping to M_{0,5}.
ideas.modern_name: 1-dimensional special locus in M_{0,5} (fixed locus of an involution)

ideas.what: Proposal to study the induced map on fundamental groupoids from the special-locus curve to M_{0,5}.
ideas.modern_name: Galois action on special loci / Grothendieck–Teichmüller and special loci
ideas.where_published: Esquisse discusses modular orbicurves and the tower in general terms

missed.claim: Explicit plan to compute the effect on fundamental groupoids of the inclusion of the involution special locus P^1∖{0,±2,∞} → M_{0,5}, within a systematic catalogue of elementary operations of the Teichmüller tower. Later realised in substance by work on Galois action on special loci, so not genuinely missed.
missed.quote: Elle s'envoie dans la multiplicité M_{0,5} — il y a lieu de regarder l'effet sur les groupoïdes fondamentaux.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Documents that Grothendieck in 1983 already treated special loci (fixed loci of finite automorphisms) as building blocks of the tower, anticipating Schneps/Collas–Maugeais. Historically interesting rather than mathematically new.

deep.surprise_reason: A routine explicit computation of a 1-dimensional special locus in M_{0,5}. The programme it serves (fundamental groupoids of special loci in the Teichmüller tower) was later developed by others; the only notable point is the early date and an arguably unnecessary removal of s = 0.
transcription_corrections: 'Changer le terme en e_i en ξe_i' is more likely 'Changer le terme en e_1 en ξe_1', with ξ a 4th root of unity.
'donc pour ξ^2μ [?], qui ne change rien' is likely 'donc pour λ+μ, qui ne change rien' (the invariant s = λ+μ is what changes sign).
'[-rigidifiées-] {+rigidifiées+}' is likely a struck-through word (possibly 'rigidifiées' or 'définies') with a replacement; meaning 'rigidifiées par la donnée de e_1'.
